title: IMAGEDEF owner edge and parent back-reference role resolution
scope: Resolve the apparent DWG IMAGEDEF parent-role conflict by separating dictionary ownership from IMAGEDEF's common parent back-reference, while keeping strict output gated pending operation and roundtrip qualification.

dwgSpecification.document: Open Design Alliance Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1

sections.2.13: Typed absolute code 4 is a soft pointer; offset codes 6/8/A/C always represent soft pointers.
sections.20.4.81: IMAGEDEF's parentHandle is labelled hard-owner, with following reactors labelled soft-pointer. This label conflicts with the physical code-C parent back-reference and must be interpreted with the separate dictionary ownership edge.

sources.title: AcDbRasterImageDef Class
sources.observation: IMAGEDEF objects are stored in the special ISM_RASTER_IMAGE_DICT and work with RasterImage entities.

sources.title: AcDbDictionary::setAt
sources.observation: When adding a dictionary entry, the dictionary is set as the entry object's owner and added to its persistent reactor list. This establishes the dictionary-to-IMAGEDEF owner edge independently of IMAGEDEF's common parent back-reference.

sources.title: AcDbDictionary::remove
sources.observation: Removing an entry removes the dictionary as owner and as a persistent reactor; the entry object remains in the database until the caller chooses to erase it. This documents dictionary membership behavior, not IMAGEDEF copy or WBLOCK semantics.

sources.title: Common Group Codes for Objects (DXF)
sources.observation: Common object group 330 is a soft-pointer ID/handle to the owner dictionary/object.

sources.title: DICTIONARY (DXF)
sources.observation: Dictionary entry target group 350 is a soft-owner ID/handle.

sources.title: AcDbRasterImage::setReactorId
sources.observation: A RasterImageDefReactor is added to the IMAGEDEF persistent reactor list, while the image entity owns the reactor object. This is a third, distinct graph role.

joinedEvidence.physicalProfile: Four hash-bound AutoCAD SAVEAS DWG/DXF pairs for AC1021/AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 resolve the IMAGEDEF parent target to the image dictionary. Each stores the IMAGEDEF-to-dictionary back-reference as code 0xC and emits the paired DXF group 330. A separate ODA File Converter AC1024 output from a locally authored DXF uses absolute code 4; it is a different producer/profile, and code 4 is also a soft pointer. The dictionary entry points to IMAGEDEF using DWG code 2 and DXF group 350. LibreDWG 0.14 independently resolves the same code/length/offset tuple and target for the four AutoCAD DWG sources.
joinedEvidence.graphInterpretation: The dictionary entry is the owner-to-owned-object edge. IMAGEDEF's common parentHandle points back to that owner dictionary as a soft pointer (absolute code 4 or offset code 0xC, DXF group 330). The dictionary's persistent reactor entry and IMAGEDEF's image-definition-reactor links are separate relationships. ODA §20.4.81's hard-owner label conflicts with the physical back-reference encoding; ODA §2.13 and Autodesk's DXF group definitions identify the back-reference role.
joinedEvidence.cohortLimit: The four releases are one AutoCAD drawing lineage and do not count as four independent producer witnesses.

implementation.change: The independent observer now returns KnownSoftPointerOwnerBackReference for the observed standard IMAGEDEF code-4/code-C profiles. Source-to-typed correlation retains the exact role and spans without labelling the wire role unknown. Strict output remains refused by a separate explicit owner-back-reference behavior gate.
